summary: Sultan Iskandar Muda International Airport (BTJ) is the principal gateway to Banda Aceh and the Aceh province on the northern tip of Sumatra, Indonesia. Named after the 17th-century Sultan Iskandar Muda of the Aceh Sultanate, the airport was heavily damaged by the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami and has since been rebuilt and modernized. It handles domestic flights across Indonesia as well as limited regional international services, particularly routes linked to Malaysia and the Middle East.
faqs:
Q: How far is Sultan Iskandar Muda Airport from Banda Aceh city center?
A: The airport is approximately 12-13 kilometers southeast of downtown Banda Aceh, typically a 20-30 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: Are there international flights from BTJ?
A: Yes, the airport handles limited international services, primarily to Malaysia (Kuala Lumpur and Penang) and some charter or pilgrimage flights to the Middle East, particularly Jeddah and Medina.

Q: What facilities are available inside the terminal?
A: The terminal offers standard amenities including cafes, shops, currency exchange, ATMs, prayer rooms, and free Wi-Fi, along with car rental and taxi counters in the arrivals area.

Q: Is the airport affected by the time zone used in Aceh?
A: Yes, Aceh observes Western Indonesian Time (WIB, UTC+7), which is one hour ahead of Jakarta and Sumatra's western regions that use UTC+7 is standard across all of Sumatra actually, but Aceh notably observes the same zone as Jakarta.
transport_tips: Taxis and ride-hailing services like Grab are available outside the terminal and offer fixed or metered fares to central Banda Aceh; agree on the fare before departure. Damri airport shuttle buses operate on select routes connecting the airport with the city center at an affordable price. Motorcycle taxis (ojek) can be a quick option for solo travelers with light luggage, but confirm pricing in advance.
